author: WP18
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on the browser main loop: the simulateInfiniteLoop unwind that destroyed a stack-allocated Game, how it was diagnosed, the heap-allocation repair, the web loop's semantic differences and how to test a host-owned loop. At TARGET the loop was rebuilt on Asyncify, so a stack Game is valid and EndRun/AfterLoop run; the timing differences still hold. The lifecycle and timestep deep dives and frame internals already carried the current loop; the diagnosis and test method are on the web deep dive as a labelled historical case.

figures.note: Corrected to TARGET: Run() suspends on the Wasm stack via Asyncify instead of registering a callback and yielding; renderer list limited to current browser identities.

concepts.text: A native Run() owns its loop, while the browser inverts control; the earlier implementation treated the yield to JavaScript like a returning call and created a lifetime bug before the first frame.
tokens: the hand-off that destroyed the game
concepts.note: Presented as a labelled historical case; current code keeps the caller alive.

concepts.section: The throw that is not a C++ exception
concepts.text: The earlier loop called emscripten_set_main_loop with simulateInfiniteLoop=1, implemented as a raw JavaScript throw 'unwind' that native Wasm exception cleanup caught, destroying a stack-local Game while the callback still referenced it.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: RunLoop now alternates EmscriptenMainLoopCallback() with an EM_ASYNC_JS await of requestAnimationFrame, and docs/emscripten-mainloop-game-lifetime.md states the stack-local contract.

target.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (RunLoop: frame body + CNA_WaitForAnimationFrame under Asyncify)

concepts.section: The throw that is not a C++ exception
concepts.text: The page built and started, then the first scheduled frame touched dead state: compilation plus module startup does not prove a viable web port.
tokens: the first scheduled frame then touched dead state

concepts.section: Reducing the failure before explaining it
concepts.text: The fault was located by rejecting a structural hypothesis (pointer adjustment across multiple inheritance) with ASan, UBSan/vptr and SAFE_HEAP reproductions and accepting a temporal one: constructor, hand-off, destructor, callback.

target.evidence: historical diagnosis method; not a TARGET fact

concepts.text: The interim repair heap-allocated the game in twelve example entry points (commit b6686bfba) and accepted process-lifetime ownership.
concepts.note: Superseded by the Asyncify loop; TARGET entry points use ordinary stack ownership (docs/emscripten-mainloop-game-lifetime.md).

concepts.text: The renderer benchmark still constructed its game on the stack and was called a regression-shaped exception.
concepts.note: Under the Asyncify loop a stack-allocated game is correct; graphics_renderer_benchmark.cpp constructs its game on the stack by design.

concepts.text: A search-based migration must end with a search for survivors, not a count of edited files.

At TARGET the repair is structural: RunLoop alternates EmscriptenMainLoopCallback() with CNA_WaitForAnimationFrame() under Asyncify, so Run() blocks, returns after exit and calls EndRun() and AfterLoop().
concepts.note: Corrected: repair is Asyncify, not heap allocation.

concepts.section: The Web loop is not the native loop
concepts.text: The web frame body ignores SuppressDraw, always runs fixed steps (IsFixedTimeStep=false not honoured), keeps IsRunningSlowly false, and caps a frame at a hard-coded 250 ms instead of MaxElapsedTime.
concepts.note: Contract gap already recorded as NEW-B2-05.

concepts.section: The Web loop is not the native loop
concepts.text: The older text said EndRun and AfterLoop are never called on the web; at TARGET Run() calls both after the Asyncify loop returns.

concepts.section: The Web loop is not the native loop
concepts.text: The web clock comes from the platform's GetTicksMilliseconds() (the older text said SDL_GetTicks) while the native loop uses the performance counter.

concepts.section: The Web loop is not the native loop
concepts.text: None of the loop differences prevents a demo from drawing, but each can change behaviour, tests, shutdown or network timing, so they belong to the compatibility contract.
tokens: which is why they belong to the compatibility contract

concepts.section: How to test a host-owned loop
concepts.text: A host-loop regression test keeps the page alive past a frame, asserts inside it that the game is alive, reports through a browser-visible verdict, and separately exercises exit and shutdown (at TARGET: Exiting, EndRun, AfterLoop, return from Run).

concepts.section: How to test a host-owned loop
concepts.text: The minimal diagnostic trace is construction, hand-off, first callback and destruction; a function that syntactically does not return may still run cleanup machinery, so ownership must follow the host's actual control flow.
tokens: ownership has to follow the host's actual control flow
